zpnbc7: Original SpanishCue text. Read to understand the experience and the decision; then go back to the details.
pjsa8j: When Paula came back from the building meeting, three neighbors asked her for a summary. One wanted to know whether the fee would go up; another needed to confirm when the repairs would begin. Paula had taken notes, but she found that some phrases were too short. «Obras lunes» didn't say whether it was an approved date or a proposal from the company.
nsd5w4: Before sending the message, she called the administrator. The administrator explained that the work could start the following Monday if the materials arrived. She also clarified that a fee increase had not yet been approved: first they had to compare two quotes. Paula corrected her notes and, in the summary, separated what had been decided from what was pending. She wrote who had given each piece of information so that the neighbors would know whom to direct new questions to.
1tqvqey: The next day, a neighbor thanked her for the precision. He had understood that the elevator would be out of service all week, but the notice said it would be closed only for some hours and that the schedules would be announced later. Paula realized that summarizing doesn't mean cutting words at random. You have to keep the conditions that change what a person can do with the information. Since then, when taking notes, she marks with a symbol the doubts she needs to confirm before becoming the group's messenger.
